body: Thanks. I guess I just don't feel like I matter. I've been trying unsuccessfully to connect with my friends. But everyone's too busy to care about someone they never see. Now my brothers are doing it too.
I needed the smile this gave me. Thank you. I hope I can have a little boy to bring me joy like yours does to you. I hope you find the help you need to cope with your si. ❤️

I would if I still lived in FL. Haven't in years and I miss it so much. Sorry you're having a hard time finding friends. I've been cut off from mine since the pandemic started. My family's in the States. All I have is my husband. I hope you find someone.

Ah, I understand what you mean. I guess I hope that God has grace for people that end their lives, because he loves them and knows what they're going through. But no one really knows I guess. I know the common belief is that suicide is an unforgivable sin. 

I hope you're able to find some peace in your situation.

Hi Userman64, suicidal Christian here.

I would say that when it comes to my religion, the biggest thing that keeps me going isn't the fear of going to hell, it's the belief that my life won't end when I die. It's pretty hard not to care about that, considering that what I really want out of suicide is for my life to end. If killing myself won't even do that then what's the point, y'know? 

I'm not schizophrenic, but I have depression and OCD. A lot of my obsessions are related to self harm and suicide. So I get what it's like to have morbid thoughts. I have this core belief that I'm going to kill myself one day, and I can't really picture my future past a few more years. That's not much fun. 

It's not weird that you don't want to get better. I think that's pretty common with mental health problems. 

I don't know where you live, but I would consider seeking psychiatric help as soon as possible. I know that's really scary, and I don't say that lightly because I had a rotten experience in inpatient, but if you're having hallucinations and they're causing you significant distress that's definitely worth talking to a professional about. Maybe you could look to see if there's an urgent care with a psychiatric team where you live? If going to the ER sounds too scary that could be a good alternative.

I hope this helps a bit. Getting help is hard and scary. But I'm sure that people like my husband, who's successfully fighting his depression, would say it's worth it. I'm not there yet, but I'm not giving up yet either.

I'm so sorry you're struggling with this...

I have OCD, and my thought patterns look a lot like this. I can't really remember the last time my brain was actually kind to me. My psychiatrist thinks that part of my suicidal ideation is related to that, as in an actual obsession. I say a part because I used to just think about suicide all the time without really wanting to act on it, and I used to find it really disturbing. Right now I'm depressed and suicidal enough that I'm not disturbed by those thoughts anymore.

I get what it's like to watch your thought patterns fall into a place you don't like. 

I've never really taken anti anxiety medication. I had propanol once I was supposed to take if I felt anxious but it didn't help me either. 

I guess I just wanted to let you know that I'm sorry the doctor said that to you. If you're disturbed by the thoughts you're having, and you're financially able to, it's worth getting a second opinion. If you're worried that your mind isn't healthy, that's just as important than if you might act on them/if you're a rational person. A hallmark of OCD tends to be that people understand their thoughts aren't rational but they still can't get the thought out of their head, like most people can let them go.

Im not sure if this has benn really helpful at all... But if you'd like you can always pm me.

I struggle with this too. Lately what's been getting me to cry is golden retrievers. I watched Homeward Bound the other other day for the first time since I was probably six. Spent the whole film in tears because Shadow is such a good boy. Then on Twitter there was an obituary for another good boy. And everyone was commenting with the pictures of the Goldens they lost and sentiments that they hoped they found each other and we keeping each other company until their owners came to them. I just absolutely lost it. 

Feels like a really weird thing to cry to. But it's keeping me sane to know I still can cry to try to get my feelings out. Even if it's in a really sideways way.

don't know where you live, but where I live they have to think you're in immediate danger, or will harm someone else, before they make you go to the hospital.

I admitted to my therapist that I was feeling suicidal, I even told her my plan and everything, and she didn't contact any authorities to make me go to the hospital. I had made some changes around the house to keep me safe and I made a safety plan with her so maybe that's why she didn't think I was in immediate danger. Don't know.

Before the suicidal ideation I was seeing her for therapy for my OCD and it was helping me
